title: Peace, Friendship, and Careful Words
overview: This chapter is a collection of short sayings about peace at home, honest speech, fair justice, loyal friendship, and knowing when to stay quiet.

parts.label: Peace over plenty (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: A plain meal in a calm home is better than a feast full of fighting, and a sensible servant can rise above a son who brings shame and even be given a share of the inheritance like a family member. As fire tests silver and gold, the LORD tests what is really in a person's heart.

parts.label: Lies, the poor, and family (vv. 4-6)
parts.note: People who do wrong like to hear lies, and mocking the poor or gloating over someone's disaster is treated as insulting the God who made the poor. Grandchildren are pictured as an old person's crown, and parents as their children's pride.

parts.label: Words, bribes, and letting go (vv. 7-10)
parts.note: Fine words do not suit a fool, lies suit a leader even less, and verse 8 simply observes that a bribe feels like a lucky charm to the one who gives it. Letting a wrong go keeps love alive while retelling it splits friends, and a wise person takes in one warning more deeply than a fool takes a hundred lashes.

parts.label: Fools, fights, and justice (vv. 11-15)
parts.note: Repaying good with evil brings trouble that stays in a household, and a fool on a rampage is worse to meet than a mother bear robbed of her cubs. A quarrel spreads like water through a cracked dam, and freeing the guilty or condemning the innocent are both called hateful to the LORD.

parts.label: Friends, pledges, and pride (vv. 16-20)
parts.note: Money cannot buy wisdom for someone with no mind for it, but a true friend stays loyal and family shows its worth in hard times. Shaking hands to guarantee a neighbor's debt could leave you paying it, and the "high gate" of verse 19 may mean showy building or proud talk, though scholars are unsure.

parts.label: Grief, joy, and quiet words (vv. 21-28)
parts.note: A foolish child grieves parents, a cheerful heart works like medicine, and bribes passed from the fold of a robe, where people carried valuables, twist justice. The wise speak little and stay calm, and even a fool can seem wise by keeping quiet.

think: When has letting someone's mistake go helped a relationship, and when might staying quiet about a wrong have done more harm than good?
